name: fda-decisions
title: FDA regulatory decisions and enforcement actions, from openFDA bulk exports

licence.name: Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal
licence.proof: openFDA's own licensing page dedicates the content to the public domain under CC0 1.0.
licence.source_statement: As noted in the terms of service, unless otherwise noted, the content, data, documentation, code, and related materials on openFDA is public domain and made available with a Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal dedication.
licence.statement_seen_in: the body of https://open.fda.gov/license/, last modified May 27, 2014, read unchanged on 2026-10-12
licence.gmdn_carve_out: The same page says GMDN Term Code, Name and Definition are supplied under licence from The GMDN Agency and need a licence from them for commercial use and for AI training purposes. drop_fields below is the gate; no endpoint in this library has a GMDN field.

robots.says: A Drupal policy for the web site. Disallows /core/, /profiles/, /admin/, /node/, /file/, /taxonomy/, /search/, /health and the /user/ paths; Disallow: / for one named agent, vspider; Crawl-delay: 2 for usasearch. Says nothing about bulk data, and this library fetches nothing from this host.

No robots.txt is served. The body is an S3/CloudFront AccessDenied page for the static site, not a policy, so there is no rule to obey and no rule to claim. This library fetches nothing from this host either; only the human-readable licence page was read, by hand, once.

No robots.txt is served. The body is the S3 XML AccessDenied, which is what that bucket returns for any key it does not hold. This is the host the bulk files come from, so: no policy is published, and the build fetches only the exact partition URLs that openFDA's own api.fda.gov/download.json advertises for download, one request per endpoint per day, nine requests in all.
No robots.txt. The body is the API app's own 'Cannot GET /robots.txt'. One request per endpoint per build, to download.json only.

source.robots_note: Three of the four hosts publish no robots.txt at all; a 403 or a 404 on robots.txt is the absence of a policy and is recorded as such, not read as permission for anything beyond the published bulk URLs. O-32 recorded the same 403 on open.fda.gov and found the same on download.open.fda.gov.

endpoints.what: One row is one FDA drug application (NDA, ANDA or BLA), with its products and its submission history.

One row is one Orange Book product: an approved drug product with its therapeutic-equivalence codes, and its patent and exclusivity entries where FDA lists them. Checked 2026-10-12: all 48,761 records carry exactly one element in products, so products[0] is the record's own product and not a choice among several.
One row is one drug recall as FDA's Enforcement Report publishes it.
One row is one 510(k) premarket notification decision.
One row is one device product code, with its class, regulation number and FDA definition.
One row is one premarket approval decision or supplement. 1,480 of them are an original PMA with an empty supplement_number; the pair is still unique across all 57,238.
One row is one device recall record from FDA's recall database, keyed on its RES number.
One row is one device recall as FDA's Enforcement Report publishes it.
One row is one food or cosmetic recall as FDA's Enforcement Report publishes it.

count_checks.why: openFDA's own total_records for this endpoint, read live from download.json, must equal the rows built
the record count download.json gives for this partition must equal the rows built
the count in the exported file's own meta.results.total must equal the rows built
every record the streaming reader saw must become exactly one row

drop_fields.why: The name of a named individual at the applicant firm, on 151,655 of 176,299 records as read 2026-10-12. Personal data is out on docs/42 section 5 and on rail 1. The decision record stays; the person's name does not.
The name of a named individual and a direct telephone number, on 52,748 of 59,468 records as read 2026-10-12. Personal data is out on docs/42 section 5 and on rail 1.

not_covered: The adverse-event endpoints: drug/event, device/event, food/event, animalandveterinary/event and cosmetic/event. They are reports about individual people, carrying age, sex, weight and medical history. Personal data is out on docs/42 section 5 and on rail 1. This build never requests them, not even to count them; the record counts printed for them above come from openFDA's own download manifest.

device/udi. Its records carry GMDN Term Code, Name and Definition, and open.fda.gov/license says GMDN content needs a licence from The GMDN Agency for commercial use and for AI training purposes. docs/42 section 5 allows CC0 and CC-BY only, so it is out.

The multi-partition endpoints that are neither of the above: drug/label (14 partitions), other/nsde (3), device/registrationlisting (2) and animalandveterinary, device and drug event files. This library is built for single-partition endpoints, so that one endpoint is one zip and the whole library rebuilds daily inside the 20-minute budget.

Single-partition endpoints outside the administrative set O-32 named: device/covid19serology, drug/ndc, drug/shortages, other/historicaldocument, other/substance, other/unii, research/*, tobacco/problem and transparency/crl. Not refused on any rail, simply not in scope for O-32.
The contact fields listed under drop_fields. The decision record is here; the named individual is not.
Any interpretation. A row is the agency's administrative record, unchanged. This library says nothing about what an approval, a classification or a recall means.
